title: Not by bread alone (Deuteronomy 8:1–3)
hookLine: the hunger in the wilderness taught them to live by every word
carry: carried, even when it didn't feel like it

cards: Four in the afternoon, and lunch never happened. First a low hum in the stomach, then a tightness, then a short answer to someone who didn't deserve it. Hunger is honest.
Now stretch that to forty years of depending, morning after morning, on food that came with the dew and spoiled if it was saved.
Moses, near the end of his life, looks back at those years in Deuteronomy, and says something surprising about the hunger. It wasn't an accident. It was a lesson.

teach.b: Moses says, in the King James Bible: "thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness."

teach.h: FIRST THE HUNGER, THEN THE MANNA.
teach.b: And then: "he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live."
Look at the order. First the hunger. Then the manna, a food nobody had ever seen, so nobody could take credit for it.
Then the lesson: you need bread, yes, and you also need something bread can't give, the word that comes from God.
Moses adds a tender detail in the next verse: in all those forty years, your clothes didn't wear out, and your feet didn't swell. Carried, even when it didn't feel like it.
Later, in the Gospels, Jesus is alone in the wilderness for forty days, fasting, and he's hungry. The tempter says: if you're the Son of God, turn these stones into bread.
Jesus answers with this verse from Deuteronomy, in slightly different words.

teach.h: MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE.
teach.b: In the King James Bible's Matthew: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God."

Christians who keep fasts, in Lent or before communion or at other times, often reach for this verse to explain them: not to punish the body, but to let a little hunger remind them what else they live on.

how: Some Christians fast at certain times, such as Lent, Fridays or before communion, and Orthodox and Catholic Christians keep set fasting days; this verse is a common way to explain why.

a food no one had seen, given each morning in the desert

games.q: what's inside the passage — tap the pairs.
p: a food their fathers never knew

s: not by bread alone first appears in the Gospels
it's Deuteronomy 8:3. Jesus quotes it back in the wilderness.
Moses says the hunger in the desert was part of a lesson
he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna.
the verse says bread doesn't matter
it says not by bread only. bread matters; it isn't all a person lives on.

games.q: you're Jesus, forty days without food in the wilderness. the tempter says, turn these stones into bread. what do you answer?
o: quote Deuteronomy: not by bread alone.
games.why: he answers with Deuteronomy 8:3: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God."

practice: Notice what you're hungry for beyond food: rest, attention, being known, a word from God.

Some people let a small hunger, one skipped snack or dessert, be the reminder; only if it's safe for you, and if you're pregnant, unwell, or have any history with food that makes this hard, skip the hunger and keep just the listening.
If you pray, turn each pang into a short prayer.
